sammendrag: This study sought to understand more about how literacy, language, and numeracy (LLN) skills gained in workplace literacy and numeracy courses are developed, utilised, and transferred within workplaces. A literature review on the transfer of workplace learning (Cameron et al, 2010) provided a framing for the analysis of six case studies that were conducted during 2010. These 'cases' were a variety of workplaces that offered LLN courses funded by the Workplace Literacy Fund and delivered by external training providers. The purpose of the research was to gain an understanding of what helps or hinders trainees in transferring skills or knowledge they learn through literacy, language, or numeracy training to other situations, such as their jobs. LLN skills are more likely to be learnt and transferred to other contexts if tutors follow good teaching practices that promote learning; if tutors help trainees practice the application of their learning in a structured way; and if trainees have plenty of opportunity to use their LLN skills outside the context of the training course. Because people learn through practice, LLN training in the workplace tends to be more effective when there are strong connections between the content of the training and the trainee's job content or job requirements.
tittel: The transfer of language, literacy and numeracy skills from learning programmes into the workplace
